_source: Ground truth read directly out of the PDF: a 2-page installation instruction for a Hoffman enclosure temperature controller, in EN/FR/ES/DE. It has NO specification TABLE, but it does state specs in prose — `Operating temperature range: -45 °C to 80 °C (-49 °F to 176 °F)`, `Rango de temperatura de empleo -45 °C to 80 °C`, `Set point on adjustment knob: 16 C (61 F)`, `required minimum temperature in enclosure: 5 C (41 F)`, `Hysteresis of temperature control: + 11 K` — plus safety prose and the footer `PH 763 422 2211 • nVent.com/HOFFMAN | 87920845 | Rev. D | P/N 87920846`.
mustNotContain: against incidental contact is to be ensured

_notes.why: Started as the pure negative fixture: a document with no spec table must not invent specs. It emitted 8 attributes, all garbage — a copyright footer parsed as `© 2018 Hoffman Enclosures Inc. = PH 763 422 2211 …`, and safety sentences split mid-clause (`The safety and protection = against incidental contact is to be ensured`). The spec-plausibility gate (P0.2#7/#8) removed those.
_notes.correction: The original note here claimed the document contains no specifications at all. That was WRONG, and widening the admission gate to the ontology (P1.1) proved it: the document states its operating temperature range in four languages, and the English-only keyword gate was hiding every one of them — including the Spanish `Rango de temperatura de empleo`. The corpus must record what the source says, not what an earlier reading assumed.
_notes.temperature: The document says -45 °C to 80 °C, and this now passes. It was a knownGap: the value reaches the normalizer as a dual-scale string (`-45 °C / 80 °C / -49 °F / 176 °F`, because an upstream miner joins alternatives with `/`) and parseTemperatureRange refused every clause stating both scales rather than risk reading Fahrenheit as Celsius (P0.2#9). P1.1c made that refusal precise: where the scales CAN be separated — each number carrying its own unit, or one column per scale — read the Celsius side; where they cannot (`Set Point (°F/°C) 32/0 to 140/60`, bare pairs) still refuse.
_notes.prose: The remaining `Feature` entries are genuine prose specs (hysteresis, minimum enclosure temperature). Keeping them is right; they are source-backed facts, just not table rows.
